purpose.text: Make sophisticated business technology feel coherent, dependable and accessible across the Dot platforms, while each platform keeps its own functional identity. This profile carries shared principles and non-negotiables only.

evidence.summary: Section 3: the ecosystem should communicate coherence, intelligence, dependability and operational capability; platforms preserve their own functional identities.

audience.description: The ecosystem spans platforms for different users (see platforms/*.md). No single ecosystem-wide audience is asserted here. Audiences belong in brand and product profiles.

evidence.summary: The ecosystem profile states shared principles only; audiences are set per brand and product.

positioning.text: Coherence, intelligence, dependability and operational capability, communicated through shared experience principles and not through a shared look. There is no shared visual identity.

evidence.summary: Section 3, "The Dot Ecosystem", and "Do not impose one generic interface on every product".

emotional_promise.text: Moving between Dot platforms feels like using one dependable system, not unrelated products.
emotional_promise.label: intended

evidence.summary: Section 3: the ecosystem should communicate coherence.

emotional_promise.text: The system is informed and helpful, and says plainly what it knows and does not know.
emotional_promise.label: intended

evidence.summary: Section 3: the ecosystem should communicate intelligence.

emotional_promise.text: The user can rely on the platform to behave predictably and to tell the truth about its state.
emotional_promise.label: intended

evidence.summary: Section 3: the ecosystem should communicate dependability.

emotional_promise.text: The user feels equipped to run real operations with the tools at hand.
emotional_promise.label: intended

evidence.summary: Section 3: the ecosystem should communicate operational capability.

behavioural_principles.text: Every data-dependent view shows distinct loading, empty, partial, stale and error states in plain language. Success is shown only after the server confirms it.
Every error offers a retry, an undo, an alternative or a named human route. Destructive actions are reversible or state their consequence.
WCAG 2.2 level AA is the baseline on every platform and outranks brand expression.
Identical concepts carry identical names, units and status words across platforms.
No dark patterns. Value is defined by user outcomes; streaks, opens and session time are not targets (brain.dopemine.md section 2).
Each platform publishes its design tokens in a machine-readable file so another platform can link to or embed it without recolouring.
Each platform keeps its own functional identity and information hierarchy. No platform copies another platform's identity to look coherent.

evidence.summary: Section 3: individual platforms must preserve their own functional identities; do not impose one generic interface.

behavioural_principles.text: Domain safety, regulation, accessibility, security and functional correctness outrank every brand rule (ADR-0021).

evidence.summary: Section 5: never allow the brand framework to override domain-specific safety, regulatory requirements, accessibility, security or functional correctness.

constraints: No shared visual identity is defined or implied at ecosystem level.
Each platform defines its own identity in its own repository.
The only thing shared visually is token interoperability: machine-readable tokens per product.
prohibited: Imposing one generic interface on every product.
Copying another platform's colour, type or layout identity as a shortcut to coherence.

voice.text: Plain, specific and calm. States what the system did, what it knows and what it does not know.

evidence.summary: A calm, factual register fits the intended feelings of dependability and intelligence.
evidence.rationale: Derived from the intended feelings and the calm-technology principles of brain.design.md section 1; those principles were written for Brain surfaces and are not shown to fit every platform.

forbidden.rule: Do not state customer counts, usage figures, testimonials, awards, partner logos or compliance and certification claims unless sourced from real, current data and cited.
Do not advertise or link features that do not work today.
Do not present estimates, predictions or machine-generated output as certain; label them.
Do not claim that users feel a particular way without evidence of an observing class.

evidence_required: any security, privacy or compliance statement

experience_standards.expression: Each platform declares its own intended feelings in its product profile. This profile names only the ecosystem-level ones: coherence, intelligence, dependability, operational capability.
Users act in their own business vocabulary and can hand outputs to third parties unchanged, on every platform.
Each platform documents its own signature decisions and keeps its own functional identity.
Honest states, sourced figures, recoverable errors and no invented proof on every platform.
Benefits are shown as results the user can check, never only asserted.
Each platform specifies and tests its own states, spacing, motion and tokens.
One question and one next action per screen. Density is for trained operators and is grouped by decision relevance.
Each product defines and instruments its own first meaningful result.
No dark patterns. Return is driven by delivered outcomes. Engagement recommendations need human review (brain.dopemine.md).
Export and cancellation are honest and easy. Retention is observed and understood, not forced.
WCAG 2.2 AA is the baseline on every platform and outranks brand expression.
Shared concepts share names and machine-readable tokens. Layouts and identities are not shared.

domain_overrides.reason: A calm or reassuring tone must never soften a safety, regulatory or loss-of-money alert. The alert wins.
Distinctive colour, type and motion yield to contrast, visible focus and reduced motion.
Demonstrated value never overrides correctness: a polished wrong figure is worse than no figure.
A faster first result must not skip identity verification, consent or security steps.

unknowns.question: No behavioural or customer evidence about how users feel about any Dot platform is held in this repository. Every emotional_promise item is intended, not measured.
Which interoperability tokens must each platform publish, and in what format? No shared token format exists in this repository today.
Where does the shared entity glossary live and who owns it? indexes/GLOSSARY.md is Dot.Brain's own glossary, not a platform-wide interface glossary.

InfoDot's PRODUCT.md refers to a dark control-room look used by Dot.Memory, Dot.Central and Dot.Projects. Whether that is an ecosystem direction or three platforms' own choices is not documented in this repository.
Per-platform audiences are not asserted here. Brand and product profiles must establish them, with evidence.
